items_missed: Never got or used the customer's name. He pulled her full profile from her email address and still never said 'Carly' once in 8.5 minutes.
No agenda statement and no 'How are you today?'. 'If that could potentially work we can kind of discuss pricing' is a signpost, not the roadmap plus 10-15 minute timeframe plus confirmation.

No Worries Damage Coverage never explained. 'Comes with everything from taxes insurance' was the only reference — the $2,000 repair/replace/reimburse figure and the 60c/lb baseline were both absent. This is the flagship differentiator reduced to one word.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned, despite him quoting a specific 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM arrival window. That window is the natural setup for 'and if we miss it we start discounting immediately.'
No deposit required never mentioned — and this was a price-sensitive customer who volunteered 'it was higher than I remember from last time.'

'No hidden fees' was asserted but not sold. He said 'there's no additional hidden fees other than that trip fee' without enumerating no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees.

Packing needs never asked. He assumed she was self-packing and jumped to 'how many boxes we thinking around like five to ten?' — she never confirmed she has boxes or is packed, which is the one variable that could push this past the minimum.

No confirmation email named. He promised a 'meet you movers email' and a 'courtesy text' the day before, but never told her a confirmation email with her booking details is coming — so the email handoff flag does not clear.

No details read back and no 'reply with any corrections.' He copy-pasted from a year-old profile — right after discovering that same profile had a trip-fee discrepancy ('it looks like the trip fee was not in the equation last time which is weird') — and never verified addresses, date, or window with her.

No comprehension check anywhere. Rate, inclusions, trip fee, clock start, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments and the $595 total all came out in one unbroken monologue; the customer's only replies were 'Mm-hmm', 'Sure', 'Okay'. No 'does that make sense?'.

Save Your Ass speech absent. Partial credit only because the 2.5-hour minimum genuinely caps the downside, but the protective half of the speech fully applied and was missed — the one thing that pushes this job past the minimum is an unpacked room on arrival.
No special considerations, walk distance, parking or driveway access asked at either address, and no traffic mention on a 78723 to 78717 cross-Austin run.
Assembly/disassembly was named as included but never framed as a time variable — on a bedroom-only move the bed frame is the time driver.
Minor efficiency drag: asked house-or-apartment and one-or-two-story twice each in the first two minutes.
top_strength: The pricing and clock mechanics were delivered cleanly and completely — $208 an hour for two movers and one truck, taxes and insurance and pad wrap included, disassembly and reassembly handled, floor and door protection, a $75 trip fee named honestly as an out-of-zone charge, the clock starting on arrival and running through transit until unload, a 2.5-hour minimum, and 15-minute increments after that, landing on a $595 number. That is the full clock section, unprompted, in one pass. Better still was how he handled the price objection: when she said 'it was higher than I remember from last time,' he didn't deflect — he pulled her history, told her straight that it was $200 an hour last time with no trip fee, and then proactively waived the $75 himself ('I'll go ahead and I'll waive it for you just because you're working with us again'), restating the number as $520. He also looked up her prior crew by email and told her Sebastian and Ben had done her last move, which she loved. That is a real rapport moment and a real save.
coaching_note: Nick, this is a mechanically strong call — you are one of the few reps giving the full clock explanation unprompted, and the trip-fee waiver was a smart, well-timed save on a customer who had just told you the price felt high. The highest-leverage fix is the No Worries pitch. You compressed our flagship differentiator into the single word 'insurance' inside a list of inclusions. Say it out loud instead: 'And you're covered by our No Worries Damage Coverage — up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse anything we accidentally damage, versus the 60 cents a pound the industry standard gives you.' That is thirty seconds and it is the reason people pick us. Second priority: you gave her a 1:00 to 3:00 arrival window and stopped there. That window is a promise — finish it with the On-Time Guarantee: 'and if we miss that window, we start discounting immediately.' Add 'no deposit required' right next to it, since she was watching the number. Third, break up the pricing monologue. Everything from the hourly rate through the $595 came out in one breath and all she could do was say 'mm-hmm' — land the rate, ask 'does that make sense so far?', then do the clock. Last thing, and it is the easiest win on this list: you had her full profile open and you never once said her name. Carly should have heard it three or four times.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and conversational with real acknowledgment of her concerns — he validated the price increase honestly, looked up her previous movers by name, and waived a fee unprompted, drawing genuine positive responses ('Okay, that was great', 'I appreciate that'); held back from a 5 by never using her name and by one long uninterrupted pricing monologue.
